ground.label: Background
ground.note: The colour behind this section. Change it between one section and the next so the page reads as bands instead of one flat colour.

plain.label: Default
plain.note: The page's own background colour. Quiet, and the right choice for most sections.

soft.label: Light
soft.note: A soft tint. The easiest way to separate one section from the one above it.

brand.label: Brand colour
brand.note: Your brand colour, with text chosen to stay readable on it. Best used once or twice a page, not on everything.

layout.label: Desktop layout
layout.note: How the header is arranged on a computer screen.

inline.label: Single row
inline.note: Logo, menu and buttons all on one row. The usual choice, and the shortest.

centred.label: Stacked
centred.note: Logo on its own line with the menu centred underneath. A more formal look, but the header is twice as tall.

menu.label: Mobile menu
menu.note: What the menu does on a phone, where the links will not fit in a row.

drawer.label: Slide-out drawer
drawer.note: A panel slides in over the page. Full height, and it scrolls on its own if you have a lot of links. What most people expect on a phone.

panel.label: Drop-down panel
panel.note: A panel drops down from the header, full width. Lighter, and best when you only have two or three links.

row.label: Scrolling row
row.note: No button at all - the links stay in a row you swipe sideways. Only works with a few short links.

sticky.label: Sticky header
sticky.note: Whether the header stays on screen as people scroll.

static.label: Off
static.note: The header scrolls away with the page, leaving the whole screen for your content.

pinned.label: On
pinned.note: The header stays at the top. People find their way around about 22% faster and your sign-up button is always there, but it takes up room on every screen.

menu-align.label: Menu alignment
menu-align.note: Which side the links line up on inside the mobile menu. It does not move the menu itself.

menu-start.label: Left
menu-start.note: Lined up on the left. Easiest to scan, and the default.

menu-centre.label: Centre
menu-centre.note: Calmer, though sub-links lose the indent line that marks them out.

menu-end.label: Right
menu-end.note: Lined up on the right, so they follow on from the button that opened them.

menu-side.label: Menu position
menu-side.note: Which side the menu button sits on. The menu opens from the same side, so the button is always beside what it opens.

side-start.label: Left
side-start.note: Button on the left, menu opens from the left.

side-end.label: Right
side-end.note: Button on the right, menu opens from the right. The default.

toggle.label: Menu button
toggle.note: Whether the button that opens the mobile menu carries a word beside the three bars. Your word is read out to anyone using a screen reader or voice control either way.

labelled.label: Word and bars
labelled.note: Your word for the menu, next to the three bars. People find it more readily than the bars on their own, so this is the safer choice and the default.

icon.label: Bars only
icon.note: Just the three bars. Tidier, and it hands room in the bar back to a wide logo. Worth it when your menu is short and your visitors know the site.

edge.label: Bottom edge
edge.note: How the header is separated from whatever sits under it. The header is exactly the same height whichever you pick.

rule.label: Hairline
rule.note: A thin line across the bottom. Quiet, works on any page, and the default.

shadow.label: Soft shadow
shadow.note: No line - a soft shadow instead, so the bar reads as floating above the page. Suits a header that stays on screen as people scroll.

flush.label: None
flush.note: Neither line nor shadow, so the header sits straight on the section below. Right when that section already has a colour or a picture of its own.
